trust_contract: Per bundle, exactly three pinned tuples: {:kind :evaluation :identity <evaluator> :intent-digest <digest> :receipt-pin <pin>}, same for :review and :authorization (kind :authorization, identity = authorizer codex-11 session 01a16136). The retained trusted-manifest.edn in each dir IS this exact set. Docstring: TRUST is independent of artifact bytes and must authenticate exact receipt scope. Nothing in the grammar authenticates a principal generally — trust is scoped to one intent-digest + one receipt pin per role.
remaining_evidence_limitations: Ordinals 41, 43, 50 are NOT clean as-is on current disk: their acceptance-contract artifacts are mutable repo test files that have drifted (41, 43) or been deleted (50) since adoption. Pinned bytes are recoverable from git (7ca70e10e, ae9e71584, 86024a594) but a naive live re-verification refuses. Any approval must pair the trust ruling with a hermetic re-pin or restore of those three files, or the composed context still fails 3 of 11.
No receipt is a cryptographic attestation (each says not-a-cryptographic-attestation). Authentication rests on file custody of the notes tree + git history, not signatures.

Authorizer for 10 of 11 is one identity (codex-11 session 01a16136…); only ordinals 38/46/48 receipts embed the operator basis (Joe instruction + coordinator-record pins). Ordinals 39,40,41,42,43,44,50,71 receipts carry no embedded operator basis — their chain rests on the directory-level coordinator records and dispatch logs, which live outside the receipts and were not all re-hashed in this packet (38/45/47 coordinator records and the shared current-clearance record WERE byte-verified today).

Root pins in each intent are the ledger root AT ADOPTION TIME (historical prefixes), not the current root; the grammar checks root-consistency of the sealed entry chain, and this holds — but approving means approving the historical prefix chain as it was then, which is exactly what the sealed entries attest.

supported_context.adoption-driver: Each adoption dir ships adopt.clj: `clojure -M adopt.clj validate` (validation-only: fresh isolated ledger copy + controls, no canonical write) and a coordinator-gated live mode (e.g. A9_LIVE_ADOPTION=coordinated) that ran the ORIGINAL appends. supported_context.composition-boundary: futon2.aif.meta-medic-authority/resolve-context validates one or more exact-scope bundles and returns an AuthorityResolution whose verifier accepts an operation only when EXACTLY ONE bundle verifies it (overlaps refused as ambiguous). Its identity is a digest-pinned scope list — no artifact bytes, no executable trust in the identity.
supported_context.can-it-express-narrow-trust: YES, grammatically: resolve-context over the 11 retained bundles (each trust = trust-from its own trusted-manifest, accepting exactly 33 pinned tuples total) accepts ONLY this pinned set — future unknown entries fail trust and refuse. It is not blanket trust of codex-11 or of any schema.
supported_context.can-it-be-installed-without-new-code: NO. There is no supported standing/persistent trust-install entry. resolve-context is process-local; nothing persists a resolved context across restarts, and the serving click boundary (full_loop_runtime.clj:121-125 :else) builds no bundle context — that is precisely the composition gap. Wiring resolve-context into the serving default is a code change (design-adjacent), NOT an operator invocation. Per dispatch: not implemented, not invented here.
